clue.text: Iris directing patriotic display

parts.note: the flag is a name for the yellow iris, a waterside plant
waving traffic along is directing it, so directing can mean waving

explanation.surface: An iris arranges a show of national pride.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a woman's name or part of the eye; here it is the plant called a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving banners is the standard showy demonstration of national loyalty, hence the idiom for jingoism.

clue.text: Unstable product of Belial

indicators.note: the letters of the name Belial are worked into something new, a product made from them

explanation.surface: Something shaky was made by the demon Belial.
explanation.walkthrough: Belial is a biblical name for the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Labile is a scientific word for liable to change or break down, i.e. not steady.

clue.text: Her patience was finally successful, says the old tale

definitions.text: Her patience was finally successful, says the old tale

parts.words: Her patience was finally successful, says the old tale
parts.note: the heroine of a medieval story told by Boccaccio and Chaucer, a wife whose endless patience under her husband's cruel tests is at last rewarded

explanation.surface: A woman's patience paid off in the end, according to legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Patient Griselda of the Clerk's Tale endures every trial and is finally restored to her husband's favour.

clue.text: All-powerful car required on Arctic trip

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters of Arctic fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A mighty vehicle is needed for a polar journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey but signals the anagram: ARCTIC rearranged gives CRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocratic ruler holds absolute power, answerable to nobody.

clue.text: List that's about times for assembly

indicators.note: the two letters for 'that's' go about, or around, the rest

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: the letters of times are to be put together afresh, assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A list of the times needed to put something together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for assembly' turns TIMES into TEMIS, which sits inside I...E, from 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set things down one by one, as in a list.

clue.text: The crew are adding angostura — just a little

indicators.note: only a small run of letters is taken from inside the words adding angostura

explanation.surface: The bar staff are putting a dash of bitters into the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a team of workers, like a road gang or a ship's crew.

clue.text: Tropical disease caused by surfeit of fruit, it is said

indicators.note: spoken out loud the words for the fruit match the disease's name

parts.note: too much fruit is a berry and another berry

explanation.surface: An illness in the tropics brought on by eating too much fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a vitamin B1 deficiency illness common in warm countries where polished rice is the staple.

clue.text: To take off, you must first put it on

definitions.text: To take off, you must first put it on

parts.words: To take off, you must first put it on
parts.note: take off sounds like undressing, but means an aircraft leaving the ground, when passengers must be strapped in

explanation.surface: Something you have to put on before you can take it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Airline passengers must fasten the restraint across the lap before the plane leaves the runway.

clue.text: Old English component of American degree is always changing its form

indicators.note: the letters for Old English become a part placed within the degree

parts.note: an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: Old English is part of an American qualification that keeps shifting shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The single-celled creature has no fixed body shape, constantly pushing out and drawing in its outline.

clue.text: Drink for sailors in the meeting

indicators.note: the sailors meet, joining up with, the words in the that follow them

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink for sailors at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green wormwood-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: Arsenal's journal

explanation.surface: The football club Arsenal's own publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal, a London football club, suggests a club magazine; but a store of weapons and ammunition is also a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store for weapons and ammunition, and a journal is a periodical publication.

clue.text: Sank port, we hear — a large amount

explanation.surface: A harbour that went down, apparently, with a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sank' sounds like cinq, French for five: Deal in Kent was attached to the Cinque Ports, a group of ancient south-coast harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kentish town belonged to the Cinque Ports confederation; 'a great deal' means much.

clue.text: Greasy Joan's successor uses powder

parts.note: greasy Joan is the kitchen maid in a Shakespeare song who scours the pots; her modern replacement is a machine fed with detergent powder

explanation.surface: The heir of a grubby woman wears make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy Joan scrubbed pans by hand; today a kitchen appliance cleans the plates using a powdered detergent.

clue.text: Constantly use telly, or disconnect it

indicators.note: breaking the words apart and putting them back differently, as unplugging a set breaks its connection

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who watches TV all the time: either use it or unplug it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something resolutely means doing it steadily and unwaveringly, without a break.

clue.text: In Bavaria they have real leather seats

definitions.text: In Bavaria they have real leather seats

parts.words: In Bavaria they have real leather seats
parts.note: seats reads like car upholstery, but it means backsides: the traditional Bavarian leather shorts

explanation.surface: Cars in Bavaria come with genuine leather upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional Alpine shorts made of leather cover the wearer's seat, i.e. bottom.

clue.text: Lift most of the secrecy

parts.note: to lift is to steal, as in shoplifting

indicators.note: all of the word the except its final letter is used

explanation.surface: Raise most of the secret thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting covertly, keeping one's movements hidden.

clue.text: Once the height of elegance, old car makes one curse

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: the top, or first letter, of the word elegance is taken

parts.note: crate is slang for a ramshackle old car

explanation.surface: An old banger, formerly the last word in style, makes someone swear.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down a curse upon something.

clue.text: It made a change for the old nudist

indicators.note: the letters of the words it made a are given a change of order

explanation.surface: Something altered things for an elderly naturist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adamites were an early Christian sect who worshipped naked, imitating the unclothed first man in Eden.

clue.text: Englishwoman in India turned out to be his mam

indicators.note: the letters of be his mam are turned out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman in colonial India proved to be the mother of a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the respectful Raj-era term for a European married lady living in India.

clue.text: This much tar can be a danger to shipping

definitions.text: This much tar can be a danger to shipping

parts.words: This much tar can be a danger to shipping
parts.note: refers to the saying about spoiling the ship by skimping on the tar, the tiny quantity worth one halfpenny

explanation.surface: A small amount of pitch can put vessels at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'don't spoil the ship for a ha'porth of tar': saving a trifle on caulking can sink the vessel. A halfpenny was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfpennyworth is the tiny amount of tar in the proverb about a ship lost through penny-pinching.

clue.text: Vehicle with swivel seat

parts.note: to wheel is to turn or swivel round
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A vehicle fitted with a revolving seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled chair for someone unable to walk is a small personal conveyance.

clue.text: Congregated round lake in thaw

indicators.note: the word for congregated goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: people who congregated met together
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: People gathered around a lake as the ice broke up.
explanation.definitionFit: Melt and thaw both mean to change from frozen to liquid.

clue.text: Candy is dandy, but this is quicker, said Ogden Nash

definitions.text: Candy is dandy, but this is quicker, said Ogden Nash

parts.words: Candy is dandy, but this is quicker, said Ogden Nash
parts.note: quotes the American humorist's couplet on seduction, comparing sweets with strong drink

explanation.surface: Ogden Nash's famous quip about what works faster than sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Nash's rhyme 'Candy is dandy, but ...' ends by naming alcohol as the quicker route to romance.

clue.text: Opera wives

explanation.surface: A two-word note about operatic wives.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's opera Die Entführung aus dem Serail is known in English as The Abduction from the Seraglio.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Abduction opera is often called simply by this name, and it also means a harem, the women's quarters of a sultan's household.

clue.text: Nothing less than prison will do for mischievous child

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is taken away from the word for prison

parts.note: limbo is old slang for prison
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Only jail will suit a naughty youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a limb of Satan' is an old phrase for a naughty child, shortened to limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A little limb is an imp or rascal, from the phrase limb of the devil.

clue.text: Presumably it's always a busy time in the Peak District

definitions.text: Presumably it's always a busy time in the Peak District

parts.words: Presumably it's always a busy time in the Peak District
parts.note: Peak District, an upland area of England, puns on peak times, the busiest travel period

explanation.surface: The Peak District national park must be busy all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is a national park in northern England; peak hours are the busiest for commuters.
explanation.definitionFit: Peak travel time is when commuter traffic is heaviest.

clue.text: Consider for prize

explanation.surface: Think about a reward.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem is to regard or deem, and also to value highly or cherish.

clue.text: Stern prohibitions in prison

parts.note: the stern is the back or behind of a ship
bars are bans or prohibitions

explanation.surface: Strict bans apply inside jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being locked up means confined within cell gratings, a common idiom for incarceration.
